points.text: Practical applicability unclear due to strong assumptions.
Empirical results are limited and toy-level.
Scheme is not a genuine discretization; assumes exact Brownian motion simulation.
Analysis largely builds on prior works; limited novelty.
Theorems are standard extensions of prior Nitanda et al. results; synthesis rather than novel.
Only one low-dimensional experiment barely showing advantage.
Lacks motivating example grounding constrained sampling in real ML problems.
Should motivate by showing new settings unlocked, e.g., weight-constrained networks or generative modeling.
Discretization cost of Step 5 unanalyzed; no discussion why it is easier than Brownian motion on X.
Proof techniques borrowed from prior papers; limited technical novelty.
Exact simulation of diffusion step assumed; gap with one-step implementation.
Discrete-time analysis only for mean-field neural network setting, limiting generality.
D is infinite for admissible mirror maps, making Theorem 4.3 bound vacuous.
Assumption 4 uses Euclidean Fisher information while proof needs mirror LSI.
Assumptions 4 and 8 never verified for any example.
'First' and 'sharpest known bounds' wording exceeds what is proved.
Experiment's barrier violates Assumption 5(i).
Experiment lacks numbers, repeats and loss definition; stability/optimality claim unsupported.
Baseline is a trivial failure case; reparametrization baseline missing.
Analysis assumes exact dual diffusion; experiments use one Euler step.
Hypothesis lists reference wrong assumptions and equations.
Misattributed OV00 citation and duplicate bibliography entries.
Typos in Sections 1.1 and 3.
Theorem 4.3 bound infinite because D is infinite for every admitted mirror map.
Assumption 4 stated with wrong Fisher information; does not give the proof step.
Uniform LSI assumptions never checked; no sufficient condition or example.
Barrier in experiment violates Assumption 5(i).
Experiment under-specified: loss estimation, target, init, horizon, repeats, numbers missing.
Experiment does not test exponential rate or 1/N particle behaviour.

Theory uses exact diffusion simulation; experiment uses one Euler step.
Theorem hypothesis lists cite wrong assumptions.
Typos, wrong equation reference, duplicate bibliography entries.

Uniform LSI assumptions not verified for any example.
Notation and hypothesis-list inconsistencies obstruct checking.
Experiment too small, no repeats or numbers to support optimality language.
No limitations paragraph.
Typos.
Technical novelty modest; most theorems repeat prior arguments.
'First' and 'sharpest' wording overstates contribution.
Missing positioning vs projected Langevin and mirror descent in measure space.
